subject: Arcadia x Redwood — design partner invite (public case study + reference calls)
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Maya Patel <maya.patel@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Wed, May 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Arcadia x Redwood — design partner invite (public case study + reference calls)
Attachments: Redwood_Customer_Reference_Program_Overview.pdf

Hi Maya,

Based on what you shared on the call re: VPC/private networking, audit logs, and key ownership, Arcadia is exactly the kind of team we’re building Redwood Private for.

Would Arcadia be open to being a design partner for a short, structured customer story + reference program?

What we’re asking for (lightweight + tightly controlled):
1) Public case study (web + PDF)
- 1–2 interviews (45 min each): one technical (platform/infra) and one business/owner perspective (optional)
- We’ll draft the narrative + diagram, then route everything for your review and approval
- We can keep it high-level on sensitive items (no subnet/VPC IDs, no vendor account details, etc.) and only include metrics you explicitly approve

2) Reference calls for qualified prospects
- ~1 call/month at most, and only for opportunities you approve
- We send a prep one-pager in advance (context + topics to avoid), and Redwood can attend to keep the conversation on safe ground

Proposed timeline (assuming your internal approvals cooperate):
- Week of May 12: kickoff + interview #1
- Week of May 19: technical validation / metrics review (we can use your existing dashboards + agreed measurement window)
- Early June: draft review with your team
- Mid/late June: publish (or we can hold until you’re ready)

If you’re open, the next step would be a 20-minute alignment call to confirm:
- who the spokesperson/champion should be
- what can/can’t be shared publicly
- your approval path (comms/legal/security)

Does next Tue/Wed work?

Best,
Avery

Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com


---

From: Dr. Maya Patel <maya.patel@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, May 7, 2025 at 2:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Arcadia x Redwood — design partner invite (public case study + reference calls)

Hi Avery,

Thanks for sending this over. Tentatively yes — I think this could be valuable, but I need to sanity-check with our security/compliance lead and comms.

A few questions:
- Public vs private: can we do an anonymized version if comms/legal pushes back on name/logo?
- Reference calls: we’d want to cap frequency and ensure we can decline specific requests. Also, we can’t discuss patient-related workloads or anything that could be interpreted as PHI.
- Metrics: we can likely share relative improvements, but absolute numbers (latency, cost) might be sensitive. How strict is that requirement?

If helpful, I can pull in our Security PM (Elena) for a quick alignment call.

I’m available Wed 11:00–12:00 PT or Thu 2:00–3:00 PT.

Maya

Dr. Maya Patel
Director, Data Platform
Arcadia Health


---

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Maya Patel <maya.patel@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: Thu, May 8, 2025 at 4:27 PM PT
Subject: Re: Arcadia x Redwood — design partner invite (public case study + reference calls)

Maya — completely aligned on all of that.

On your questions:

1) Anonymized option
Yes. We can do:
- “Arcadia Health” named + logo (best case)
- named but no logo
- fully anonymized (“Large US healthcare org”) with no identifying details
We’ve done all three, depending on customer comms policies.

2) Reference call boundaries
Also yes. The program is opt-in per request:
- You can cap frequency (e.g., 1 per quarter) and/or only participate during a defined window
- You can decline any request for any reason
- We’ll send a short prep sheet ahead of time and will explicitly list “do not cover” topics
And we will not ask you to discuss anything involving patient data / PHI. We can keep reference calls focused on platform criteria (deployment model, audit logs, key management, reliability, rollout/fallback, etc.).

3) Metrics / quantified outcomes
We prefer a measurable outcome, but it doesn’t have to be absolute numbers if that’s sensitive. Options we’ve used:
- percent improvement (e.g., “reduced p95 latency by ~X%”)
- bounded ranges (e.g., “sub-second p95 on typical prompts”) with a clear definition of the test
- non-performance outcomes (e.g., “met internal audit logging requirements,” “reduced incident volume via fallback policies,” “accelerated deployment approvals”)
If you’re willing, we can propose language and you can redline it down to what’s acceptable.

Let’s do Wed 11:00–11:30 PT and please include Elena (or anyone else who needs to bless the boundaries). If you send the invite, I’ll accept.

One more thing: for the public version (if you choose named), there’s usually a simple quote/logo release at the end — but we only start that once the draft is in good shape and your team is comfortable.

Thanks again — excited to collaborate.

Best,
Avery

Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com
